title: Critical Pedagogies and Artificial Intelligence: Teaching, Curriculum, and Sustainable Education
extended_summary:
This book chapter volume addresses how artificial intelligence can be integrated into higher education curricula and teaching practices in ways that support sustainable development goals. The central problem is how to move from isolated AI tools in education to a more coherent framework that links machine learning, deep learning, pedagogy, institutional change, ethics, and sustainability. The authors position AI as a transformative technology for personalization, assessment, tutoring, analytics, and curriculum design, while also emphasizing risks such as bias, privacy, inequity, and overreliance on automation.

The work is based on a systematic literature review approach using PRISMA guidelines and searches across major scholarly databases. Rather than studying a single intervention with participants, it synthesizes existing literature on AI applications in higher education, including adaptive learning systems, intelligent tutoring systems, predictive analytics, automated assessment and feedback, virtual/augmented reality, language learning tools, career guidance systems, chatbots, and AI-enabled platforms and infrastructure.

The intended context is higher education institutions, especially universities and colleges developing AI-enhanced curricula and support systems. The main conclusions are that effective AI integration requires strong institutional support, technical infrastructure, faculty development, governance, ethical safeguards, and alignment with sustainability goals. The chapter argues that AI can improve personalization, inclusion, efficiency, and educational quality, but only if implemented in a human-centered and responsibly governed way.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative/book chapter with a systematic-review flavor, but it does not present a primary empirical design, comparison groups, or reproducible effect estimation. The chapter synthesizes prior work and offers conceptual recommendations rather than original causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues for broad institutional and pedagogical benefits of AI in education, but it reports no original quantitative impact and provides no effect sizes. Its practical implications are potentially useful, yet the evidentiary basis here is indirect and unclear.

interventions.use_case: Narrative, review-based synthesis of AI integration in higher education curricula for sustainable development, covering machine learning, deep learning, intelligent tutoring, predictive analytics, automated assessment, chatbots, and related institutional platforms rather than evaluating one implemented system.

finding.finding_summary: The chapter argues that AI integration in higher education can improve institutional quality, equity, scalability, and sustainability through personalized learning, predictive analytics, automated assessment, and AI-enabled student services. No primary empirical effect sizes are reported; the evidence is synthesized from prior literature and framed as institutional-level benefits contingent on infrastructure, governance, and faculty development.
finding.measure: Narrative synthesis of institutional outcomes including quality of education, equity/access, scalability, sustainability, and readiness for implementation

finding.finding_summary: The chapter repeatedly states that AI can reduce teacher workload by automating grading, feedback, student support, engagement analysis, and administrative tasks. However, these claims are descriptive and do not report original quantitative estimates such as time saved or effect sizes.
finding.measure: Teacher workload, grading efficiency, student support efficiency, and administrative automation described in the review

finding.finding_summary: The review suggests AI-supported personalization and adaptive systems may improve student engagement, inclusion, and persistence, especially for diverse or at-risk learners. These are not tested outcomes in this chapter; no sample sizes or effect sizes are reported.
finding.measure: Student engagement, inclusion, and retention as discussed in the literature review
